news.headline: US Fed Hikes Rates 25 bps to 5.25-5.50%; Markets Recover Pre-Market
news.what_happened: The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate 25 bps on Sep 17 to 5.25-5.50%. US markets fell intraday (S&P -0.5%, Dow -1.2%) but pre-market Sep 18 shows sharp recovery: S&P +1.14%, Nasdaq +1.69%, as markets now price this as the terminal or near-terminal hike. US 10Y yield fell from 5.006% to 4.947% overnight.
news.why_it_matters: Falling 10Y yield signals bond market believes the rate hike cycle is near its end. This boosts risk-on sentiment globally, driving FII flows into EMs. Nasdaq +1.69% is a strong tailwind for Indian IT sector valuations. Banking sector also benefits from lower yields boosting bond portfolio values.

news.headline: Saudi Arabia Restoring 50% East-West Pipeline Capacity; Crude Softens
news.what_happened: Saudi Arabia announced partial restoration of its East-West crude pipeline (damaged by drone attacks last week), restoring roughly 50% capacity within days. WTI crude fell -0.54% to $101.36/bbl; Brent fell -0.71% to $104.08/bbl.
news.why_it_matters: Supply restoration eases geopolitical risk premium. Lower crude is a marginal tailwind for Indian industries with crude-linked input costs (airlines, paints, tyres, chemicals). However, at $101 WTI, crude remains elevated. OMC and upstream oil producers face mild headwinds from inventory loss and lower realizations.

news.headline: FII Net Sellers Rs 3,208 Cr; DII Net Buyers Rs 3,618 Cr on Sep 17
news.what_happened: Foreign Institutional Investors were net sellers of Rs 3,208.80 Cr in cash segment on Sep 17, while Domestic Institutional Investors (LIC, mutual funds) absorbed the selling with net purchases of Rs 3,617.80 Cr, a near-complete offset.
news.why_it_matters: DII support prevented a sharper market sell-off. With US markets recovering pre-market, FII sentiment may shift positive today. Market resilience despite Fed hike and FII selling is a structural positive signal for Indian equities.

news.headline: Asian Markets Gain: Nikkei +0.76%, Hang Seng +0.77%
news.what_happened: Japanese Nikkei rose to 64,626 (+0.76%) and Hong Kong Hang Seng gained to 24,794 (+0.77%) on Sep 18, tracking US pre-market recovery.
news.why_it_matters: Positive Asian session signals broad regional risk-on sentiment. FII re-entry into Indian equities more likely. Metals and mining get a mild lift from Hong Kong/China proxy momentum.

picks.catalyst: Nasdaq +1.69% overnight recovery; US Fed terminal rate narrative strengthens as 10Y yield falls to 4.947%
picks.logic: TCS derives ~55% revenue from North America. Nasdaq +1.69% signals tech sector re-rating and improved discretionary IT spend outlook in the US. US 10Y yield falling from 5.006% to 4.947% reduces discount rate for growth stocks, lifting IT valuations. TCS closed at Rs 2190, near flat on Sep 17, meaning no pre-positioning. High FII ownership (~18%) makes TCS a natural re-entry target as global risk-on resumes.

picks.catalyst: Oversold on Fed hike fear (fell -1.18% on Sep 17); US rate hike now delivered and seen as near-terminal; US 10Y yield falling; DII buying support
picks.logic: HDFCBANK fell from Rs 721.5 to Rs 713 (-1.18%) on Sep 17 as markets priced in Fed rate hike risk. With the hike now delivered and US 10Y yield declining, rate-sensitive sectors should mean-revert. RBI holds repo at 5.25% with neutral-to-easing bias; DII net buyers of Rs 3,617 Cr provide floor support. HDFCBANK is India's largest private bank with highest FII ownership — a natural re-entry target as sentiment turns risk-on.
